claim: HLJ1 knockout mice show reduced organ injury during LPS-induced endotoxic shock.

claim: HLJ1 deletion affects IFN-γ-related gene signatures in distinct immune cell clusters under LPS stimulation.

claim: Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection.
source: Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection (Singer et al., 2016).
evidence: Cited from Singer et al., 2016.

claim: Sepsis is the single most encountered cause of death in intensive care patients.
source: In intensive care patients, sepsis is the single most encountered cause of death (Mayr et al., 2014).
evidence: Cited from Mayr et al., 2014.

claim: Both pro- and anti-inflammatory responses occur early and simultaneously in sepsis.
source: Although sepsis is a biphasic disorder characterized by an initial hyperinflammatory phase followed by an immunosuppressive phase, studies have shown both pro- and anti-inflammatory responses occur early and simultaneously where the net effect of the competing process is typically dominated by a hyperinflammatory phase featuring shock and fever (Hotchkiss et al., 2013; Munford and Pugin, 2001; Kurosawa et al., 2011).
evidence: Cited from Hotchkiss et al., 2013; Munford and Pugin, 2001; Kurosawa et al., 2011.

claim: The net effect of competing inflammatory processes in sepsis is typically dominated by a hyperinflammatory phase featuring shock and fever.
source: Although sepsis is a biphasic disorder characterized by an initial hyperinflammatory phase followed by an immunosuppressive phase, studies have shown both pro- and anti-inflammatory responses occur early and simultaneously where the net effect of the competing process is typically dominated by a hyperinflammatory phase featuring shock and fever (Hotchkiss et al., 2013; Munford and Pugin, 2001; Kurosawa et al., 2011).
evidence: Cited from Hotchkiss et al., 2013; Munford and Pugin, 2001; Kurosawa et al., 2011.

claim: Immune response in sepsis features protracted, unabated inflammation driven by the innate immune system, leading to organ dysfunction and mortality.
source: Investigators have recently proposed that immune response in sepsis features protracted, unabated inflammation driven by the innate immune system, leading to organ dysfunction and even mortality (Xiao et al., 2011).
evidence: Cited from Xiao et al., 2011.

claim: Septic shock is the common cause of death in ICU and is usually caused by systemic Gram-negative bacterial infection.
source: Septic shock contributing to failure of vital organs and hypotension is the common cause of death in ICU and is usually caused by systemic Gram-negative bacterial infection (Chiche et al., 2011).
evidence: Cited from Chiche et al., 2011.

claim: Engagement of LPS to TLR4 in macrophages results in downstream expression of proinflammatory cytokines such as IL-1, IL-6, IL-12, and IL-18.
source: Engagement of lipopolysaccharide (LPS), the membrane component of bacteria, to TLR4 in macrophages transduces signals to intracellular proteins, resulting in downstream expression of proinflammatory cytokines such as IL-1, IL-6, IL-12, and IL-18 (Beutler and Rietschel, 2003).
evidence: Cited from Beutler and Rietschel, 2003.

claim: IL-12 produced by APCs activates natural killer cells.
source: Produced by APCs (antigen-presenting cells), IL-12 activates natural killer (NK) cells and induces the differentiation of naive CD4+ T cells to become IFN-γ-producing Th1 effector cells in responses to pathogens (Schenten and Medzhitov, 2011).
evidence: Cited from Schenten and Medzhitov, 2011.

claim: IL-12 induces the differentiation of naive CD4+ T cells to become IFN-γ-producing Th1 effector cells in response to pathogens.
source: Produced by APCs (antigen-presenting cells), IL-12 activates natural killer (NK) cells and induces the differentiation of naive CD4+ T cells to become IFN-γ-producing Th1 effector cells in responses to pathogens (Schenten and Medzhitov, 2011).
evidence: Cited from Schenten and Medzhitov, 2011.

claim: Secreted IFN-γ augments IL-12 production by priming IL-12p40 gene promoter in APCs in a positive feedback loop.
source: In a positive feedback loop, secreted IFN-γ augments IL-12 production by priming IL-12p40 gene promoter in APCs (Grohmann et al., 2001).
evidence: Cited from Grohmann et al., 2001.

claim: The IL-12/IFN-γ axis-mediated communication between innate and adaptive immunity plays an important role in the control of infections by mycobacteria and other intracellular bacteria such as Salmonella.
source: The IL-12/IFN-γ axis-mediated communication between innate and adaptive immunity plays an important role in the control of infections by mycobacteria and other intracellular bacteria such as Salmonella (Ramirez-Alejo and Santos-Argumedo, 2014).
evidence: Cited from Ramirez-Alejo and Santos-Argumedo, 2014.

claim: In models of sterile sepsis and chronic bacterial infection, the IL-12/18-IFN-γ axis is controlled by ARTD1 in myeloid cells, contributing to TH1 response and immune control of bacteria.
source: In models of sterile sepsis and chronic bacterial infection, the IL-12/18-IFN-γ axis is controlled by ARTD1 in myeloid cells, contributing to TH1 response and immune control of the bacteria (Kunze et al., 2019).
evidence: Cited from Kunze et al., 2019.

claim: IFN-γ knockout mice showed lower levels of IL-6 and MIP-2 in the circulation during CLP-induced septic shock.
source: However, the pathogenic role of IFN-γ has been implicated during CLP-induced septic shock where IFN-γ knockout mice showed lower levels of IL-6 and MIP-2 in the circulation and are resistant to CLP-induced mortality when treated with systemic antibiotics (Romero et al., 2010).
evidence: Cited from Romero et al., 2010.

claim: IFN-γ knockout mice are resistant to CLP-induced mortality when treated with systemic antibiotics.
source: However, the pathogenic role of IFN-γ has been implicated during CLP-induced septic shock where IFN-γ knockout mice showed lower levels of IL-6 and MIP-2 in the circulation and are resistant to CLP-induced mortality when treated with systemic antibiotics (Romero et al., 2010).
evidence: Cited from Romero et al., 2010.

claim: Inhibition of IFN-γ activity by neutralizing antibodies improves survival and attenuates CLP-induced sepsis in rat.
source: The inhibition of IFN-γ activity by neutralizing antibodies improves survival and attenuates CLP-induced sepsis in rat, while it does not reduce CLP-related mortality in mice (Romero et al., 2010; Yin et al., 2005).
evidence: Cited from Romero et al., 2010; Yin et al., 2005.

claim: Inhibition of IFN-γ activity by neutralizing antibodies does not reduce CLP-related mortality in mice.
source: The inhibition of IFN-γ activity by neutralizing antibodies improves survival and attenuates CLP-induced sepsis in rat, while it does not reduce CLP-related mortality in mice (Romero et al., 2010; Yin et al., 2005).
evidence: Cited from Romero et al., 2010; Yin et al., 2005.

claim: Heat shock proteins can be upregulated under cellular-stress conditions such as oxidative stress, hypoxia, fever, and inflammation.
source: Heat shock proteins (HSPs) can be upregulated under cellular-stress conditions, such as oxidative stress, hypoxia, fever, and inflammation, and they act as chaperones to maintain the functions of cytosolic proteins (Georgopoulos and Welch, 1993; Rosenzweig et al., 2019).
evidence: Cited from Georgopoulos and Welch, 1993; Rosenzweig et al., 2019.

claim: Heat shock proteins act as chaperones to maintain the functions of cytosolic proteins.
source: Heat shock proteins (HSPs) can be upregulated under cellular-stress conditions, such as oxidative stress, hypoxia, fever, and inflammation, and they act as chaperones to maintain the functions of cytosolic proteins (Georgopoulos and Welch, 1993; Rosenzweig et al., 2019).
evidence: Cited from Georgopoulos and Welch, 1993; Rosenzweig et al., 2019.

claim: HLJ1 is a member of heat shock protein 40 family and is also known as DNAJB4.
source: Human liver DnaJ-like protein (HLJ1) is a member of heat shock protein 40 family (HSP40) and is also known as DNAJB4.
evidence: Stated as background information.

claim: HLJ1 is a tumor suppressor in non-small-cell lung cancer and colorectal cancer.
source: In humans, HLJ1 is a tumor suppressor in non-small-cell lung cancer and colorectal cancer, since its upregulation suppresses tumor invasion and high expression of HLJ1 is associated with prolonged survival of patients (Liu et al., 2014; Tsai et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2005).
evidence: Cited from Liu et al., 2014; Tsai et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2005.

claim: Upregulation of HLJ1 suppresses tumor invasion.
source: In humans, HLJ1 is a tumor suppressor in non-small-cell lung cancer and colorectal cancer, since its upregulation suppresses tumor invasion and high expression of HLJ1 is associated with prolonged survival of patients (Liu et al., 2014; Tsai et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2005).
evidence: Cited from Liu et al., 2014; Tsai et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2005.

evidence: Cited from Reitberger et al., 2017.

source: Dnajb4+/+ and Dnajb4−/− mice showed similar survival rates when LD50 dose of LPS (10 mg/kg) was used (Figure 1A)

claim: Dnajb4−/− mice were significantly more resistant to LPS-induced sepsis and exhibited longer survival than Dnajb4+/+ mice when subjected to a higher lethal dose of LPS (20 mg/kg).
source: but Dnajb4−/− mice were significantly more resistant to LPS-induced sepsis and exhibited longer survival than Dnajb4+/+ mice when subjected to a higher lethal dose of LPS (20 mg/kg) (Figure 1B).

claim: Serum aspartate transaminase (ALT) levels were slightly reduced in Dnajb4−/− mice at 8 hr after LPS injection.

claim: The quantities of both HDL and LDL were slightly reduced at 4 hr post-LPS injection, but there was no difference between the two genotypes.

The quantities of both lipoproteins were slightly reduced at 4 hr postinjection, but there was no difference between the two genotypes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).

claim: HLJ1 deletion does not confer increased susceptibility to IFN-γ.

claim: Serum levels of IL-6 were slightly lower in Dnajb4−/− mice than in Dnajb4+/+ mice after LPS challenge.

claim: Enrichment analysis of significant genes from LPS-injected Dnajb4+/+ and Dnajb4−/− mice revealed differential expression in MHC class-I-related signals in macrophages.

claim: HLJ1 enhanced sepsis death via IL-12 regulation.

source: Because mice are rather insensitive to LPS (Cauwels et al., 2013), we use high-dose LPS (20 mg/kg LPS) which can resemble sepsis-induced SIRS and severe endotoxemia (Silva et al., 2019) to induce endotoxic shock.

claim: LPS-induced endotoxemia cannot represent actual sepsis as it is the host's response to bacteria but not the pathogen itself that leads to mortality and organ failure.

claim: HLJ1 inhibition combined with systemic antibiotics might be a promising strategy to treat sepsis.
